# Bundled WPE source and downstream patch policy

`upstream.json` pins the WPE WebKit **2.54.0 release archive** by URL and SHA-256.
It does not assert an unverified upstream Git commit. `patches/series` lists
reviewable downstream patches in application order. The series is currently
empty; no request-broker API has been implemented.

Permitted patches provide generic embedding capabilities. Public APIs, source,
tests and patch subjects must not contain application/extension-specific concepts.
UXP is never part of this series. Record each patch's purpose, upstream base,
changed files, added API, default/unopted behavior, tests and upstreamability in
this directory. No manual unlisted edits to the extracted WebKit source are allowed.

## Verify

```sh
python3 tools/wpe/test-verify-source.py
python3 tools/wpe/verify-source.py --allow-python-cache
```

Verification first checks the pinned archive hash. It constructs expected patched
files from the archive in a temporary directory, applies the series with
`git apply --check` and `git apply`, and compares every source entry. Contents,
executable bits, symlink targets, deleted files and unexpected additions are
checked. Unlisted or duplicate patches fail. Symlink/gitlink and binary patches
are deliberately unsupported. Source under test is never repaired or modified.

The release archive repeats some paths; the last member at a path wins, matching
normal extraction. This is not an allowance for edits in the source tree.

The optional flag allows generated `__pycache__/name.cpython-N[.opt-N].pyc` files
only when their source `.py` module is itself in the verified inventory. No source
file is excluded. Without that flag, these generated extras fail verification too.
The build wrapper sets `PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX` to the object directory, so it neither
uses those pre-existing source-side caches nor generates new caches in the vendor
tree. Generated bytecode is not a downstream source patch or shipped runtime file.

## Reproduce a patched source directory

Verify the archive hash against `upstream.json`, extract it into a **new** working
directory, then apply the listed patches in order with `git apply` from that source
root. Use absolute paths to each patch. Run the verifier with `--source` pointing
to the resulting directory. Do not reapply patches to an already modified tree,
reverse arbitrary edits to make a check pass, or overwrite a running build's files.

`tools/wpe/build-runtime.py` runs this verification before configuring/building or
installing. `--source-archive` can select another local copy of the **same pinned
archive**. Updating the upstream version is an explicit pin/series review.

The verifier establishes source provenance, not binary reproducibility or runtime
correctness. A new patch still requires build, upstream-style API tests, embedding
integration tests, race/timeout tests and pre-fetch server-counter tests. No such
broker success is claimed by a passing source audit.
